description: One-way ratchet on ESLint warnings, counted by scripts/run-lint.mjs from a single ESLint run. totals.warningCeiling replaces the hand-typed --max-warnings number that used to live in package.json: it is the exact measured count, may only fall, and is the value npm run lint enforces. perRule freezes each rule at its own count so a drawdown in one rule cannot silently pay for a regression in another - removing 500 `any` annotations while adding 500 react-hooks/exhaustive-deps warnings is a net loss that a single total would report as progress. step is the drawdown unit: when measured warnings sit a full step under the ceiling, scripts/audit-lint-warnings.mjs asks for the gain to be locked in. Lower a ceiling in the same change that removes the warnings - leaving headroom lets it refill silently.

notes.@typescript-eslint/no-explicit-any: Exactly the type-escape backlog seen from ESLint: 9039 = the 9041 in config/type-escape-boundaries.json minus its 2 suppressions, which are not an ESLint rule. The binding gate for this rule stays config/type-escape-boundaries.json, which freezes every file individually and is therefore strictly stronger than a repository total. This ceiling exists so the two cannot disagree - it must be lowered whenever the type-escape ceiling is.
notes.errorCeiling: Zero and permanent. ESLint errors are not part of the drawdown; the ratchet governs warnings only.
notes.no-empty: The 3 that remain are in client/src/pages/Payroll.tsx, client/src/pages/StockEntryHistory.tsx and client/src/pages/factory/FactoryShippingContainers.tsx. Documenting an empty catch costs two lines under this Prettier config, which pushes each of those files past its frozen god-file cap, so the cleanup is blocked until they are split - see Phase 4 of docs/god-file-split-program.md. Raising a god-file baseline to absorb it is what working rule 1 forbids.
notes.no-useless-escape: The 2 that remain are the deliberate <\/script> escapes in client/src/pages/StockEntryHistory.tsx. Removing the backslash lets the literal end an enclosing script block early; the fix used elsewhere - a SCRIPT_CLOSE constant - adds lines that file has no room for under its god-file cap.
